controls.name: fxDelayTime
controls.doc: The FX delay's time travel. `max` is the NATIVE ring's ceiling — the same number as `OMX_FXDELAY_MAX_MS` in `omx_delay.h`, pinned to it by the engine's conformance test. Distinct from the per-route ALIGNMENT delay (`OUTPUT_DELAY_RANGE`, 1 s, `OMX_DELAY_MAX_MS`): one is a musical echo with feedback and mix, the other is a pure latency. Two facts, two rings, two ceilings — sharing the word "delay" is why they keep being confused for each other.

controls.name: fxDelayFeedback
controls.doc: The FX delay's REGENERATION travel — how much of the wet tail feeds back in. Stops short of 1: unity feedback is a runaway the kernel hard-clamps anyway, so offering it would draw travel the DSP refuses. Not NORMALIZED_RANGE for exactly that reason — it is a 0..1 quantity whose top the DSP does not accept, and a control must not offer a value its actuator will eat.

controls.name: tone
controls.doc: The FX delay's TONE — a NORMALIZED_RANGE instance with its own come-up value, matching the console's delay default tone. See REVERB_SIZE_RANGE for why this is a named constant rather than a default on the shared shape.

controls.name: mix
controls.doc: The FX DELAY's wet/dry — the same split as REVERB_MIX_RANGE, its own declaration.

controls.name: pingpong
controls.doc: The FX delay's PING-PONG switch: on cross-feeds the two legs' feedback, so each leg's repeats come from the other leg's damped tap and the echoes bounce L<->R (`omx_delay.h`'s `struct omx_fx_delay.pingpong`, read where the feedback is formed). A live control on the console's delay row (`DelayState.pingpong`) and on the omx-delay plugin. Its come-up value is FX_DELAY_PINGPONG_DEFAULT, by reference, so the default keeps one home.

controls.name: fxDelayTaps
controls.doc: How many integer read taps of the FX delay's one ring are engaged. 1 is the one-tap delay, bit for bit; `max` is the tap-array ceiling the kernel sizes its arrays by, so the arrays and the travel are one fact. An array extent is an integer constant: the C reader takes OMX_FX_DELAY_TAPS_RANGE_MAX (4) for `OMX_FXDELAY_MAX_TAPS` in `omx_delay.h`, never the alias OMX_DELAY_TAPS_MAX, which is the float 4.0f.

controls.name: sync
controls.doc: Where the delay time comes from: free, the time control in ms; tempo, the division at the host's tempo, 60000 / BPM x the division's beats. It comes up free, so a fresh delay is the one that shipped.

controls.name: division
controls.doc: The note value the time follows while sync is tempo: 1/1 to 1/16, each straight, dotted (x 3/2) and triplet (x 2/3), in beats of a quarter note (DELAY_DIVISION_BEATS, in this order). It comes up a quarter.

controls.name: mode
controls.doc: The repeats' colour, in the order of the integer the kernel reads: digital, the delay as it shipped, bit for bit; tape, a one-pole low pass at DELAY_TAPE_LP_HZ in the loop and a slow wow (DELAY_TAPE_WOW_HZ, DELAY_TAPE_WOW_MS deep) on the read head; analog, a lower loop low pass at DELAY_ANALOG_LP_HZ and the soft saturation x / (1 + |x|) in the feedback. It comes up digital.

controls.name: duckDb
controls.doc: The wet's ducking depth, dB: the deepest the repeats go while the dry is loud (omx_duck: max(depth, min(0, T - L)) on the dry's level). 0 ducks nothing, the come-up value, bit for bit.

controls.name: duckThresholdDb
controls.doc: The dry level the ducking starts at, dBFS.

controls.name: duckReleaseMs
controls.doc: How fast the repeats come back once the dry falls, ms: the dry follower's release; its attack is FX_DUCK_ATTACK_MS.

DELAY_TAP_LIMITS.doc: The legal range of each read tap's gain (0..1) and pan (-1..+1, the balance law's travel), keyed by the delay row's own field, with each tap's come-up value. Tap 0 comes up at unity gain, centre: the one-tap delay. Taps 1..3 come up as a usable triple pattern (an eighth left, a dotted eighth right, a dotted quarter centre), so raising the tap count is musical at once.

FX_DELAY_PINGPONG_DEFAULT.doc: The FX delay's PING-PONG come-up value — a toggle, so it has no travel, only this. Declared here rather than as a literal in the console's delay default state (which now reads it) so the DPF plugin generator (omx-plugins) reads the same fact the desk seeds a fresh strip with.

DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_NUMS.doc: The numerators of the FX delay's tap factor set, in member order: 1/4, 1/3, 3/8, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 1, 4/3, 3/2, 2, 3. A read tap k >= 1 sits at the base time times numerator / denominator (DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_DENS at the same position), formed in double and bounded in milliseconds to FX_DELAY_TIME_RANGE.max by `omx_fxdelay_tap_ms`, then rounded once to samples. The set is two integer lists, not a set of ids, because a factor such as 1/2 is no id the schema accepts and the ratio must stay exact (1/3 has no finite decimal).

DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_DENS.doc: The denominators of the FX delay's tap factor set, in member order, one per numerator of DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_NUMS: the factor at position i is DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_NUMS[i] / DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_DENS[i].

DELAY_DIVISION_BEATS.doc: The beats each division of the delay lasts, in the order of its ids: whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth, each straight, dotted (x 3/2) and triplet (x 2/3). A quarter note is one beat.

DELAY_TEMPO_FALLBACK_BPM.doc: The tempo a synced delay reads until its host hands it one, BPM.

FX_DUCK_ATTACK_MS.doc: How fast a wet duck follows its dry key up, ms: the follower's attack, one for every effect that ducks its wet (the delay, the reverb).

DELAY_TAPE_LP_HZ.doc: The corner of the tape mode's one-pole low pass in the loop, Hz: each repeat a little darker than the last.

DELAY_TAPE_WOW_HZ.doc: The tape mode's wow rate, Hz: the read head's slow drift.

DELAY_TAPE_WOW_MS.doc: The tape mode's wow depth, ms: the read head drifts between the time and the time plus this.

DELAY_ANALOG_LP_HZ.doc: The corner of the analog mode's one-pole low pass in the loop, Hz: lower than tape's, a bucket-brigade's dark repeats.
